stops.title: Launch
stops.description: Start of the route at the AARC dock.
stops.action: Launch cleanly, check traffic, and settle onto the correct side before adding pressure.

stops.title: Downstream
stops.description: Orientation cue for the downstream direction from the dock.
stops.action: Use this cue to orient yourself before rowing away from the dock.

stops.title: Fallen Tree
stops.description: Fallen tree hazard near the rowing line.
stops.action: Look early and give the tree room without crossing into the wrong traffic lane.

stops.title: River Turn
stops.description: Downstream turn cue for the small round below the bridges.
stops.action: Come under control early, turn as coached, check traffic, and keep the turn compact.

check.question: What is the safe river-turn sequence?
choices: Stop, turn, check traffic, then cross or continue as directed.
Keep rowing through the turn and correct after you cross.
Move to the middle early and wait there.
check.feedback: A river turn is a controlled stop-turn-check maneuver. It is not a speed move.

stops.title: River Turn
stops.description: Downstream turn cue near the hard no-row area. Treat this as a place to slow down and prepare before the danger boundary.
stops.action: Set up early and turn before the no-row boundary. Do not drift toward the danger area.

stops.title: River Turn
stops.description: Companion turn cue on the Argo side of the downstream turn pattern.
stops.action: Finish the turn sequence only after checking traffic and staying clear of the no-row area.

stops.title: Island + Weeds
stops.description: Island and weed area where oars can catch if you crowd the edge.
stops.action: Give the island and weed edge room while still staying in the traffic pattern.

stops.title: River Turn
stops.description: Return-side turn cue for the small round below the bridges.
stops.action: Use the same stop-turn-check habit before settling back into the normal traffic side.

stops.action: Do not follow the bridge shape blindly; correct early so you avoid the branches.

stops.action: Do not use this side of the pillar. Choose the safe opening early.

stops.title: Pass here
stops.description: Preferred bridge opening or passing side.
stops.action: Use this cue for the safe bridge opening or passing side, then settle back into the normal traffic pattern.

check.question: At the bridge, what should you do once you identify the safe opening?
choices: Commit early to the marked opening and keep the line predictable.
Stay undecided until the shell is under the bridge.
Move toward the center so either opening remains possible.
check.feedback: Bridge decisions need an early, settled line. Last-second corrections are risky.

stops.title: Sharp Turn
stops.description: Sharper turn where it is easy to drift across the river.
stops.action: Set the turn early, stay on your side, and avoid drifting across the river.

check.question: What should you prioritize at this sharper turn?
choices: Stay close enough to your side without drifting across.
Let the boat run wide to the other side.
Speed up so steering feels easier.
check.feedback: This sharper turn requires early steering and a predictable line.

stops.title: Current
stops.description: Current can push the shell off line here.
stops.action: Expect drift here. Make small early corrections and keep your line predictable.

check.question: What changes when current pushes the shell?
choices: Make small early corrections and keep your line predictable.
Wait until the boat has drifted, then make one large correction.
Move into the middle of the river until the current passes.
check.feedback: Current is easier to manage with early, small steering corrections.

check.question: What is the safe line through this corner?
choices: Stay on your side and avoid drifting across the river.
Cut across to make the corner shorter.
Stop in the middle until the corner clears.
check.feedback: Corners are where drift becomes easy. Stay predictable and hold your side.

stops.title: Docking
stops.description: Docking works best as a slow angled approach, not a head-on approach.
stops.action: Approach slowly at an angle, make small corrections, and avoid pointing the bow straight at the dock.

check.question: What is the safest docking approach?
choices: Approach slowly at an angle, then make small corrections.
Aim straight at the dock and stop at the last second.
Come in fast so the boat keeps tracking straight.
check.feedback: Docking should be slow and angled. Do not aim the bow straight at the dock.
